Charleston housing and neighborhoods

Charleston is West Virginia's capital and biggest city, laid out along the Kanawha River at the mouth of the Elk. It is the seat of Kanawha County. The 2025 estimate puts the population at 46,117, down from 48,864 in 2020 and 85,796 at the 1960 peak. Urban renewal in the 1960s cleared many buildings, the Triangle District especially, and some vacant lots from that era remain.

Fifteen named neighborhoods fill the city, among them the East End and Edgewood historic districts, the West Side, South Hills, Kanawha City, Elk City, Fort Hill, Forest Hills and North Charleston, plus Charleston Heights, Louden Heights, Riverview, Shadowlawn, South Park and South Ruffner. House age and flood exposure shift from one to the next, so give the neighborhood when you ask a city office about an address.

Government and health care anchor jobs here. Charleston Area Medical Center, formed in 1972 from the major hospitals, serves southern West Virginia, and the chemical industry is far smaller than it once was.

Flood risk and floodplain rules

Of everything about the local setting, flooding does the most to shape a sale. The city's floodplain office counts 13 floods larger than the 1 percent annual chance flood, the last in 1934, and smaller events have done damage too. The Floodplain Manager reviews building permits and can tell you whether an address sits in a Special Flood Hazard Area. In those areas flood insurance is typically required.

An Elevation Certificate from a surveyor or engineer can help set premiums and can back a map amendment request. Charleston is the only municipality in West Virginia in the Community Rating System, at Class 9, which earns a 5 percent premium discount. Water in the Kanawha River above 123,000 cubic feet per second floods low-lying areas, and flow above 155,000 floods the mapped flood zones.

Start with the city floodplain management page and the state's flood hazard tool. Run any address before you price the house, since buyers and their lenders will.

Permits and repairs before you sell

Construction in Charleston needs a permit before work starts. The Building Department lets homeowners do their own work if the permit is pulled and an inspection shows the work meets code. Roofs, replacement windows, siding, fences, retaining walls, driveways, plumbing, electrical and HVAC all fall under the rule.

  • Permit fees are waived when the total job cost is $2,500 or less.
  • A contractor who starts without a permit pays at least $100 or twice the normal fee, whichever is greater, and faces a license suspension of at least three months.
  • A demolition permit calls for an asbestos report and details on capping the storm and sewer laterals.
  • Applications go to the Permit Coordinator, Building Department, 915 Quarrier Street, Suite 5. The permit office number is 304-348-6833.

These rules cover repairs you make to get ready for a sale, and a buyer's inspector may ask about any work done without a permit. A cash sale skips most of that back and forth, because the buyer takes the house as it stands.

Who bills and who values your home

The county bills property tax here, not the city. The Kanawha County Sheriff's Tax Division collects, and the Kanawha County Assessor sets values.

OfficeAddress and hoursPhone
Kanawha County Sheriff's Tax Office409 Virginia Street East, Room 120, Charleston, WV 25301; Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 5:00304-357-0210
Kanawha County AssessorKanawha County Courthouse, 409 Virginia Street East304-357-0250

The tax office also runs detachments in Cross Lanes, Sissonville, Elkview, Jefferson and Quincy. It mails roughly 100,000 real estate tickets and 95,000 personal property tickets every July.

Due dates, discounts and tax classes

Kanawha County uses the state calendar. Tickets go out on or after July 15, and each half is due on September 1 or March 1. Pay before either date for a 2.5 percent discount. Halves turn delinquent on October 1 and April 1, and late tax draws 9 percent interest a year.

Class matters for the rate. Owner-occupied residential property is Class II, taxed at two times the Class I rate. Other property inside a municipality, a rental for example, is Class IV at four times the Class I rate. Ask the assessor which class your house carries before you work out what a buyer will owe.

Transfer tax and other closing costs

The main government charge at closing is the transfer tax recorded with the deed. West Virginia Code 11-22-2 sets it at $1.10 per $500 of value, kept by the county since July 1, 2025. An additional county tax of 55 cents per $500 applies unless the commission has raised it, and a $20 fee covers transfers for consideration.

The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the deed with the tax unpaid. Overdue property tax, an earlier mortgage and any liens come out of the proceeds, so ask the sheriff's office for the tax status before you accept any number.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Charleston houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How a sale usually goes

Older houses, homes near the Kanawha and Elk rivers, and inherited properties are the situations sellers in Charleston plan for most. The East End and Edgewood carry historic district designations, and river-side homes raise the flood questions above.

You can list, sell by owner or sell for cash, and each route treats those issues differently. A listing brings showings and buyer financing. A cash sale usually means a title search, payoff of any liens and a deed recorded with the county. Before you pick, bring these to the first conversation:

  • your most recent tax ticket and the sheriff's balance
  • the deed, and the probate paperwork if the house was inherited
  • any permit records for work done on the house
  • a floodplain determination if the house sits near water

At closing the title company pays off liens and open tax from your proceeds, the deed goes to the county for recording, and you receive what remains. If a payoff turns out larger than you expected, you will want to learn that before you sign a contract, not at the table.

Compare what each route leaves you after taxes, liens and transfer costs, and not the headline price alone.

Roads, transit and schools

Interstates 64, 77 and 79 cross Charleston, and the West Virginia Turnpike ends at the southeastern edge. U.S. 60 and U.S. 119 run through the center. Yeager Airport is about two miles north of the interstates on route 114, Amtrak's Cardinal stops in the city, and the Kanawha Valley Regional Transportation Authority runs the buses.

Kanawha County Schools runs the public schools. Call the district to confirm the school assignment for a specific address.

Frequently asked questions

Does the City of Charleston or Kanawha County collect property tax?

Kanawha County does. The Sheriff's Tax Division at 409 Virginia Street East takes payments, and its phone number is 304-357-0210.

Do I need a permit for a roof or window replacement in Charleston?

Yes. Roofs and replacement windows are on the Building Department's permit list, and fees are waived only when the total job cost is $2,500 or less.

How can I tell whether a Charleston house is in a flood zone?

Ask the city's Floodplain Manager for a determination, or use the state's flood hazard tool. A property in a Special Flood Hazard Area typically needs flood insurance, and an Elevation Certificate can help with premiums.

What transfer tax applies when I sell a Charleston house?

The base rates are $1.10 per $500 of value plus 55 cents per $500 for the county, plus a $20 fee, unless the Kanawha County Commission has raised its rate. The seller pays unless the buyer takes the deed with the tax unpaid.

When do Kanawha County property tax payments come due?

September 1 and March 1, with a 2.5 percent discount for paying before each date. Unpaid halves turn delinquent on October 1 and April 1 and accrue 9 percent interest.

Huntington at a glance

Huntington stands on the south bank of the Ohio River, where the Guyandotte joins it, in West Virginia's southwest corner. It is the Cabell County seat, with small pieces of the city reaching into Wayne County. The 2020 census counted 46,842 people, and the 2024 estimate is 44,942, the second biggest in West Virginia. Numbers have fallen in every census since 1950, when the city held 86,353.

Collis P. Huntington founded the town in 1871, and it grew as a rail, river and steel center until the Great Flood of 1937. Health care and education carry the job base today: Marshall University, Cabell Huntington Hospital, St. Mary's Medical Center, Amazon, DirecTV and the City of Huntington. St. Mary's has more than 2,600 employees and is the largest private employer in the county. People relocating for those jobs sometimes need a fast closing.

Streets run in a grid, with avenues beside the river and numbered streets running north and south. Locals speak of four sections, split by the CSX tracks and by First Street.

  • Downtown and the Marshall campus
  • West Huntington, Old Central City and Westmoreland on the west side
  • Ritter Park, South Side, Enslow Park and the Southeast Hills to the south
  • Walnut Hills, Guyandotte, Highlawn and Forest Hills on the east side

Name your section when you talk to a buyer, because values and house age differ across them.

Do floods and weather affect a sale?

The Ohio River explains the flood walls. The Great Flood of 1937 killed five people and left tens of thousands homeless, and the walls went up in 1938. Buyers and lenders still ask about flood zone status, so look up your address on the state's flood map tool before you list.

Winters bring about 19.8 inches of snow a season, and a typical year has about 24 afternoons at 90 degrees or more. That points an inspector toward the roof, the gutters, the cooling system and the pipes and heating on the coldest days. None of it makes a house unsellable, but roof, basement and heating condition are what a buyer will price in.

What rules apply to rentals?

Owners with tenants face the city's rental registry and inspection program. A 2018 city ordinance requires rental units to meet building, fire, health, safety and zoning codes, and the city's rental inspection page explains the process. A 2020 housing report found 6,050 of 9,603 rental units, or 63 percent, in decline.

  • A one or two family rental gets at most one inspection per unit in any 12 months.
  • Inspectors look at electrical safety, heating, smoke alarms, handrails and general upkeep.
  • Tenants can request an inspection without the landlord's permission.
  • Larger buildings, with more than two units, are reviewed by the building, electrical and plumbing inspectors plus the fire marshal.

An open violation or an unregistered unit can slow a conventional buyer's lender. Someone paying cash can often buy with those items still open. For code complaints about vacant or neglected property, the Public Works office is at 304-696-4414. Registry fees have included a $75 inspection fee and a $20 business license, so call the city for current amounts.

Property tax in Cabell County

Cabell County taxes Huntington homes. The Cabell County Assessor values them and the Sheriff's Tax Office collects. The assessor's FAQ page gives 2026 levy rates for owner-occupied homes of 1.6752 inside the City of Huntington and 1.3552 in the rural part of the county. Barboursville and Milton residents pay their own city rates as well.

West Virginia sorts property into classes. Class 2 is owner-occupied residential, and Classes 3 and 4 cover property the owner does not live in. A house you move out of and rent or leave empty is assessed differently, which often surprises heirs.

InstallmentPay byCounted late on
Fall halfSeptember 1October 1
Spring halfMarch 1April 1

Bills go out on or after July 15. Paying before either due date earns a 2.5 percent discount, and overdue amounts carry 9 percent yearly interest. See the state due dates.

A homestead exemption is open to owners 65 or older with two straight years of West Virginia residence. Apply between July 1 and December 1. It removes the first $20,000 of assessed value from the bill.

Transfer tax at closing

Moving a deed triggers a state excise tax, and that is the main tax at closing. Section 11-22-2 of the state code charges $1.10 on every $500 of value, and the county keeps it. A second county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 also applies, and a county commission may raise it by vote to a maximum of $1.65 per $500.

The seller pays as grantor, unless the buyer agrees to accept a deed on which the tax is still owed. The clerk also collects a $20 fee for the state Affordable Housing Fund when property transfers for consideration. Your county's actual combined rate may differ from the base figures, so ask the County Clerk, who records deeds in Cabell County and keeps a deed lookup.

A house passing by will or by a list of heirs is outside the tax under section 11-22-1, which matters for inherited homes.

Who sells for cash in Huntington

Sellers who consider a cash sale usually share one problem: a house that would take time and money to ready for a listing.

  • Heirs holding an older home in Old Central City, Guyandotte or the South Side that nobody wants to maintain
  • Landlords whose units fail a city inspection and who cannot fund the work
  • Owners relocating for a hospital or Marshall University job on a short timeline
  • Homes with a damp basement, an aging roof or an outdated furnace that would draw repair demands from an inspector

With cash there is no bank appraisal and no haggling over repairs after the inspector visits. Cash Home Buyers reviews each Huntington property individually, and an offer depends on condition, location and the work the house needs. Decline the number and you owe nothing.

Before you accept any offer, ask that a West Virginia title company or attorney handle the closing, confirm who pays the transfer tax, and get the payoff on any mortgage or tax lien in writing.

Roads and getting around

Interstate 64 and US 60 shape how buyers see the city. Exits 6 through 15 of I-64 serve Huntington, and US 52 connects at exit 6. US 60, part of the historic Midland Trail, follows the river through downtown and splits into Third and Fifth Avenues.

The Huntington and Ashland metro area covers seven counties in three states and holds an estimated 368,000 people, so buyers and renters often come from across the river. The assessor's page links to the Tri-State Transit Authority and the Greater Huntington Park and Recreation District, handy references for an out of town buyer.

Frequently asked questions

How fast can I sell my house in Huntington, WV?

Often faster than a listing, since no lender is waiting on an appraisal. The real clock is title work and recording at the Cabell County Clerk, so ask for the closing date in writing before you sign.

Do I pay a transfer tax when I sell in Huntington?

Usually, and the seller normally pays it. Expect $1.10 per $500 of value plus a county excise tax starting at 55 cents per $500. An inheritance by will or list of heirs is outside the tax.

What happens to my Huntington rental if it fails an inspection?

The city requires the landlord to correct violations found at a registered rental inspection. Selling is the other route: a buyer paying cash may take it as is, though you should disclose known problems and run the sale past your title company.

When are Cabell County property taxes due?

Payments are due September 1 and March 1, and a 2.5 percent discount rewards early payers. Unpaid first and second halves are delinquent on October 1 and April 1.

Can I sell a house in Huntington that I inherited?

Yes, after you hold legal authority to convey the title, which usually means the estate has been opened with the county. Your title company will list the papers the deed needs.

Morgantown at a glance

Morgantown is the seat of Monongalia County, on the Monongahela River near the Pennsylvania line and about 75 miles south of Pittsburgh. The 2020 census counted 30,347 residents, and the 2024 estimate is 30,490, making it the third-largest city in West Virginia. The metro area holds about 140,000 people. The city itself is small, 10.62 square miles, with Charleston roughly 156 miles to the southwest.

Several neighborhoods began as separate towns and were annexed as the city grew. Some of them lie partly or fully outside the limits even though everyone says Morgantown. The common ones:

  • First Ward, Second Ward and South Park near downtown
  • Sunnyside and Wiles Hill beside the downtown university campus
  • Evansdale, Greenmont and Woodburn
  • Suncrest, South Hills and North Hills
  • Sabraton, the Mileground and Easton, in part or entirely outside the city

A house with a Morgantown mailing address can sit outside the city limits, and that decides which rules apply to it. Ask the city and county offices about your exact address.

West Virginia University and the buyer pool

WVU is the biggest force in the local economy and in who buys or rents a house. Enrollment tops 25,000, and the city hosts about 30,000 students, about the same as its year-round population. WVU Medicine supported 56,224 jobs statewide in fiscal year 2024, so the health system adds to the demand.

Just north of downtown, Sunnyside is an older neighborhood with a long record of student housing. A house in or near it is often valued as a rental, not a family home, and the buyers lean toward investors. If your house is a student rental with a lease running, give any buyer the lease dates up front, since they set when a buyer can take possession.

Gutters, grading and basement moisture come up in most inspections in a humid climate, and snowfall averages 27.6 inches a year. A recent roof or drainage repair is worth mentioning to buyers.

Rental registration and inspection

Rentals inside city limits go on a registry and get inspected on a schedule. The city's rental information page sets inspections at once every three years using the International Property Maintenance Code, and the owner has to fix whatever turns up. The Code Enforcement office focuses on safe buildings and rental units. Housing codes came from city officials and City Council from 1979 until 1989, when West Virginia adopted its first official written housing code.

Rental ruleWhat it means for you

Before you sell a student rental, pull your registration and your last inspection result. A violation that is still open will not block a sale, though a conventional buyer can use it as leverage. An investor paying cash can usually take on the repair list, which leaves price as the main question.

Property tax in Monongalia County

Two county offices handle the bill: the assessor sets the value and the Sheriff's Tax Office collects. Whoever owns the property of record on July 1 is the one assessed. If you sell after that date, the tax year still shows you as owner, so agree with the buyer in the contract on how the current bill will be split or paid at closing, and tell the title company.

Statements are mailed in July, and delinquent real estate tax is sold in November. The statewide calendar covers the rest:

  • Tickets are issued July 15 or later.
  • Half is due September 1, the other half March 1.
  • A 2.5 percent discount rewards payment before either date.
  • Late balances grow at 9 percent interest yearly.

For questions about paying real estate tax, call the Sheriff's tax department at 304-291-7244. An unpaid tax lien can complicate a sale, so have the title company check the status early. See the state due dates and the sheriff's tax page.

What closing costs to expect

Expect one big government charge, the state's transfer excise tax. Section 11-22-2 sets $1.10 per $500 of value, and a county commission can raise the county's added 55 cents per $500. The seller, as grantor, normally pays, and a $20 fee goes to the state's Affordable Housing Fund. The deed's stated value and your county's current rate control the final amount.

A will or an intestate list of heirs is excluded under section 11-22-1.

Listing the house the traditional way adds agent commissions, repair requests after the inspection and monthly carrying costs while it waits for a buyer. Selling to Cash Home Buyers is meant to skip those steps. What they offer depends on the property, and you owe nothing if you turn it down.

Roads, transit and airports

I-79, I-68, US 19, US 119, WV 7 and WV 705 serve Morgantown, and commuters pay attention to which one a house is near. The Mountain Line Transit Authority runs most bus service, and its Grey Line operates every day of the year between Clarksburg and Pittsburgh International Airport. The Morgantown Personal Rapid Transit system has five stations, Walnut, Beechurst, Engineering, Towers and Medical, over 8.65 miles.

  • Morgantown Municipal Airport is about 3 miles northeast of downtown on US 119.
  • North Central West Virginia Airport is about 35 miles away by road.
  • Pittsburgh International is about 80 miles away.

Describe your house's access to these routes plainly and let the buyer judge.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Morgantown houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How a quick sale works here

A cash sale in Morgantown is short. Tell the buyer the address and condition, wait for the review, and weigh the offer. Once you say yes, a title search looks for liens and open tax, payoffs are taken from what you receive, and the deed gets recorded with the county.

Get a target closing date in writing and find out which title company will handle the deed. Gather these papers first:

Cash tends to close sooner than financing, since no bank is in the queue. Paperwork is what holds things up: an unrecorded heir transfer, an open tax balance, or a tenant whose lease outlasts the planned date. Flag each one early and get the fix in writing.

  • your latest tax statement and the sheriff's balance
  • rental registration and last inspection result, if the house is a rental
  • lease dates for any tenant who stays through closing
  • the deed, or probate papers if you inherited the house

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a rental house in Morgantown with open code violations?

Yes. The city requires owners to correct violations found at inspection, but an investor paying cash may buy the property as is. Check the registration and your latest inspection result first so the title company has the facts.

Who collects property tax in Monongalia County?

The county sheriff's tax office takes the money for real estate and personal property, while the assessor sets the value. Statements go out in July, and delinquent real estate tax is sold in November.

Is a house outside the Morgantown city limits treated differently?

Possibly. The Mileground, Easton and parts of Sabraton are partly or entirely outside the limits, so ask the city and county offices which rules cover your address.

Do I owe transfer tax if I inherited my Morgantown house and sell it?

The tax applies to your sale deed to the buyer. Receiving the house by will or through a list of heirs is excluded, but the later sale is not.

How quickly can a cash sale close in Morgantown?

It depends on title work and recording, not on a lender. Request a target date in writing and name the title company that will record the deed.

Parkersburg and its neighborhoods

Parkersburg is the Wood County seat, where the Little Kanawha River meets the Ohio. The 2020 census counted 29,738 residents, fourth in the state, and the Parkersburg and Vienna metro area holds 89,490. Numbers have fallen in every census since 1960, when the city had 44,797. The city covers about 12.35 square miles.

The Little Kanawha splits the city into a north side and a south side. South Parkersburg was its own city until it joined in 1950. Most named neighborhoods are on the north side, and each has its own housing style:

  • Downtown, Julia-Ann Square and Quincy Hill
  • Beechwood, Fairview Heights and Granada Hills
  • Meadowcrest, Oakwood Estates and Woodland Park
  • Riverside, Worthington and the East End

South of the river, the former city of South Parkersburg runs into suburban southern Wood County: Blennerhassett, Lubeck and Washington to the southwest and Mineral Wells to the southeast. Some of those sit outside the city, so tax and code rules differ by address.

Chemicals, finance and federal work drive local jobs. DuPont, Highmark, United Bank and Woodcraft are known employers, and the U.S. Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service employs more than 2,000 people here. Jobs like these bring people in and out of the area, which is part of why homes change hands. West Virginia University at Parkersburg adds some rental demand.

Floodwall zone and fees

The Parkersburg Floodwall shields low parts of the city along the Ohio and Little Kanawha rivers, and owners inside the protected zone pay a maintenance fee. Article 783 of the city code treats those owners as the users and beneficiaries of the wall, who bear the cost of its continuance, maintenance and improvement. It also sets a payment schedule and penalties, and the Director of Finance administers it. The city's codified ordinances carry the full text.

Floodwall ruleWhat the city code provides
Protected flood zoneProperties at or below about 624 feet above sea level, protected by the floodwall

If you are selling inside the zone, ask whether any floodwall fees are unpaid, since the code carries penalties, and have the title company check whether a balance affects the closing. Any address can be checked on the state's flood map tool.

Vacant or neglected houses

The city's Code Enforcement Division enforces building, health and safety, zoning and nuisance codes. Its aim is voluntary compliance from owners, with further steps when that fails. See the division's page.

A separate Building Enforcement Agency meets on the first Monday of each month at 9:00 a.m. The Mayor, the City Engineer and the Code Enforcement Director sit on it, and it works on neglected, vacant and abandoned properties. State law backs this up: West Virginia Code section 8-12-16c lets a municipality set up a vacant building registration and maintenance program by ordinance.

  • Keep grass and exterior debris under control while a house sits empty.
  • Answer any notice from the division in writing and keep a copy.
  • Ask the division about open complaints before you sign a sale contract.

An heir who inherits a neglected house and cannot pay for repairs may find a direct sale simpler than a repair schedule. Cash Home Buyers looks at each Parkersburg property as is, with no obligation if you decline an offer.

Why is my house taxed as non-residential?

Wood County assesses and taxes Parkersburg property, and you pay real estate tax at the Wood County Sheriff's office, not the Assessor. The Assessor values property as of July 1. Your bill is a levy rate times your assessed value, which is 60 percent of market value. The legislature sets levy rates for the Board of Education, the county commission and the municipalities.

Two rules catch owners off guard:

  • A home deeded to an LLC cannot be taxed as Class 2 residential, so all LLC-owned property is Class 3 or 4.
  • Class 2 requires an owner-occupied home with the owner's name on the deed, so a relative living in another home you own does not qualify.

Either one can change the bill a buyer expects, so ask the assessor how your house is classed before you list.

For an inherited house, the original owner's classification may no longer apply once the home is empty or rented. Call the Assessor's office, give the parcel details and ask what class applies today, then pass that answer to anyone who makes an offer.

Due dates and the transfer tax

State dates apply. Bills issue on or after July 15, the first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. Pay early for a 2.5 percent discount, and late amounts carry 9 percent annual interest. The Tax Division page has the schedule.

At sale, the transfer excise tax under section 11-22-2 is $1.10 per $500 of value. A county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 is added, and counties can raise it. The seller normally pays, and a $20 fee goes to the state Affordable Housing Fund.

Selling from out of state

Many sales here involve an heir who lives elsewhere. Title companies can handle signing by mail or remote notary, so you rarely need to travel. Confirm who is arranging the closing and how the deed will be recorded, and keep a short list of what you need from the county before you start.

  • the latest tax statement and the sheriff's balance
  • any open notices from Code Enforcement
  • floodwall fee status, if the house is inside the zone
  • the deed or probate papers

On closing day the title company pays off any mortgage, floodwall balance and tax owed from your proceeds, the deed is recorded with the county, and the remainder is sent to you. If you cannot attend, ask that the documents be mailed to you or signed before a remote notary in advance, and get the payoff figures in writing a few days ahead so nothing surprises you at the end.

A cash buyer takes the house as it stands, so you skip arranging repairs, showings and a lender's timeline from a distance. Compare what a sale leaves after taxes, liens and transfer costs, and decline any offer that does not work for you.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Parkersburg houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Highways, rail and the airport

Interstate 77 and US 50 are the main highways, and WV routes 2, 14, 47, 68, 95 and 618 also pass through the city. The Mid-Ohio Valley Regional Airport has three flights a day on weekdays from Charlotte. Passenger trains stopped in the 1960s, with Amtrak's Shenandoah running from 1976 to 1981, and CSX still provides freight service.

Frequently asked questions

Does the Parkersburg floodwall fee affect my sale?

It can if your property is inside the protected flood zone. Article 783 of the city code puts the maintenance cost on those owners and sets penalties, so ask the city's finance office whether anything is unpaid before closing.

Who do I call about code problems on a vacant Parkersburg house?

The city's Building and Code Enforcement department handles building, health and safety, zoning and nuisance codes. Contact it before you sell so any open notice is known.

Why is my Parkersburg house taxed as non-residential?

West Virginia allows Class 2 residential status only for an owner-occupied home with the owner's name on the deed. A house deeded to an LLC is taxed as Class 3 or 4.

When are Wood County property taxes due?

The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with delinquency starting October 1 and April 1. Pay the Wood County Sheriff, not the Assessor.

Can I sell a Parkersburg house if I live out of state?

Yes. Title companies can handle signing by mail or remote notary. Confirm who is arranging the closing and how the deed will be recorded.

Selling in Wheeling?

Wheeling and its older houses

Wheeling is the Ohio County seat and the largest city in the Northern Panhandle, strung along the Ohio River about 11 miles west of Pennsylvania. The 2020 population was 27,062, fifth in the state, and the metro area holds 139,513. Parts of the city lie in Marshall County. The city covers 16.01 square miles.

It grew early. Wheeling was the end of the National Road, the Suspension Bridge opened in 1849, the Baltimore and Ohio arrived in 1853, and the city served as state capital from 1861 to 1870 and again from 1875 to 1885. Population peaked at 61,659 in 1930 and has dropped since heavy industry faded. Prosperous families built fine houses in those years, especially on Wheeling Island, and many of those homes remain. Ask for a full condition review of any older Wheeling house.

The named neighborhoods run to dozens, and the hillsides and the island make very different settings:

  • Wheeling Island, in the middle of the Ohio River
  • North Wheeling, East Wheeling, South Wheeling and Center Wheeling
  • Warwood, Woodsdale, Oakmont and Pleasant Valley
  • Oglebay Park, Park View and Wheeling Heights
  • Arbordale, Pleasanton, Springdale and Dimmeydale

Benwood, Mozart, Mount Olivet and Sherrard are partly or mostly in Marshall County, so an address that says Wheeling may be billed by a different county. Confirm the county before you look up taxes. In a historic area, ask Building and Planning whether exterior changes need review, since the city has a North Wheeling Design Review process and a Historic Landmarks Commission.

Flood zones

Flood zones are common in Wheeling. Property along the Ohio River, Wheeling Creek and its larger tributaries lies in the flood zone, and every ward has some. Check an address on the state's flood map tool.

The city's Building Code Official also serves as floodplain manager, and the department lists NFIP floodplain development guidelines on its building code services page. A fence in the floodplain needs a building permit, a detail owners often miss.

Learn your flood zone status before you accept an offer, since lenders and insurers use it. A buyer paying cash is less tied to those requirements, but a later buyer will ask the same question.

Vacant buildings and demolition

Wheeling requires owners of vacant structures to register them, and neglected buildings can be ordered repaired or razed. The Vacant Structure Code, passed by City Council in 2009, tracks ownership and encourages upkeep. Once a building is registered, the owner has a year to renovate and occupy it, tear it down or sell it before a fee starts, and the fee rises for each year the building stays vacant.

The Building Code Services page covers enforcement. Owners must maintain or raze their buildings. A careless owner may receive a Raze or Repair Order, and ignoring it can mean a Municipal Court appearance and a monetary penalty. Where public health and safety are at risk, the city may raze the structure and place a lien for the cost, without taking ownership.

  • A registered vacant building gets one year before fees start.
  • Fees rise each year the building stays vacant.
  • A city demolition becomes a lien against the property.

An owner can sell within the first year without a fee, so a prompt sale can stop the clock. If you inherited a vacant Wheeling house, learn that early. Cash Home Buyers reviews houses as is, including ones that need major work, and you owe nothing if you decline.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Wheeling house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What permits and codes apply to repairs?

The city uses the 2018 International Building and Residential Codes and the 2018 International Property Maintenance Code, with the 2020 National Electric Code. A building permit costs $4.00 per $1,000 of job cost, rounded up to the next $1,000. A new electric service adds a $25 residential fee.

Most applications are reviewed within 48 hours, and larger projects can take up to a week. Roofing, siding and window permits can sometimes be issued the same day. These are the jobs sellers commonly consider before listing:

  • A new roof, siding or kitchen and bathroom renovation
  • Electrical upgrades and new decks
  • Garage or carport construction
  • Fences in the floodplain or over 7 feet
  • Retaining walls over 48 inches

Unpermitted work can surface in a buyer's inspection and slow a sale. The city also cannot use federal community development funds for repairs on pre 1970 construction because of lead based paint rules, so do not count on a city repair grant. A buyer who purchases as is avoids that repair path altogether.

Property tax and deadlines

The Ohio County Sheriff's Tax Office collects real estate and personal property tax, and the County Assessor values the property. The tax office is at 1500 Chapline Street, Room 206. See the office page. Statements are mailed in July.

DateWhat happens
September 1First half discount ends
October 1First half becomes delinquent and interest begins
March 1Second half discount ends
April 1Second half becomes delinquent
April 30Unpaid tax is subject to publication and added fees
October 31Unpaid delinquent real estate tax is certified to the state auditor

You can search records and pay online at wvpropertytaxes.com. The office lists a $1.00 fee for electronic checks and $1.00 plus 2.2 percent for cards.

Statewide, assessed value is 60 percent of market value. Owners 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, can exempt the first $20,000 of assessed value of an owner-occupied home. See the Tax Division exemption list.

Transfer tax at closing

West Virginia taxes the deed through a transfer excise tax, which the seller normally pays. Section 11-22-2 sets $1.10 for each $500 of value, plus a county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 that a county commission can raise, and a $20 fee for the Affordable Housing Fund. The Ohio County Clerk records deeds.

A transfer by will or through a list of heirs is excluded under section 11-22-1. Before closing, ask the sheriff's office for the tax balance, since any amount owed is paid from your proceeds. Bring the deed and, for an inherited house, the estate papers.

Roads and transit

I-70 and I-470 run through the city and link it with Pittsburgh's suburbs and Ohio, and US 40, US 250 and WV Route 2 also serve it. The Fort Henry Bridge carries I-70 across the river, and the interstate passes under Wheeling Hill through the Wheeling Tunnel. The county runs the Wheeling Ohio County Airport. The Robert C. Byrd Intermodal Transportation Center is the hub for Greyhound and for regional bus service run by the Ohio Valley Regional Transit Authority.

Frequently asked questions

What happens if my Wheeling house has been vacant for over a year?

Under the city's Vacant Structure Code, registered owners get a year before a fee is assessed, and fees rise each year the building stays vacant. Selling is one of the allowed ways to resolve it.

Is my Wheeling house in a flood zone?

Every ward contains flood zones, mostly along the Ohio River, Wheeling Creek and larger tributaries. Enter your address in the state flood map tool to check.

When are Ohio County property taxes due?

The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. The halves become delinquent on October 1 and April 1.

What is a Raze or Repair Order?

It is a notice from the city's Building Inspection division requiring an owner to repair or demolish a building. Ignoring it can lead to Municipal Court and a lien for the city's demolition cost.

Who pays transfer tax on a Wheeling sale?

The seller normally pays unless the buyer accepts the deed without it being paid. The state rate is $1.10 per $500, with a county tax starting at 55 cents per $500.
